verses.zh: 那时，所罗门将以色列的长老和各支派的首领，并以色列的族长，招聚到耶路撒冷，要把耶和华的约柜从大卫城―就是锡安―运上来。
verses.en: [NOTE:1] Then Solomon convened in Jerusalem[NOTE:2] Israel’s elders, all the leaders of the Israelite tribes and families, so they could witness the transferal of the ark of the Lord’s covenant from the City of David (that is, Zion).[NOTE:3]
notes: The Old Greek translation includes the following words at the beginning of ch. 8: “It so happened that when Solomon finished building the Lord’s temple and his own house, after 20 years.”
For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

Heb “Then Solomon convened the elders of Israel, the heads of the tribes, the chiefs of the fathers belonging to the sons of Israel to King Solomon [in] Jerusalem to bring up the ark of the covenant of the Lord from the City of David (it is Zion).”

verses.zh: 以他念月，就是七月，在节前，以色列人都聚集到所罗门王那里。
verses.en: All the men of Israel assembled before King Solomon during the festival[NOTE:1] in the month of Ethanim[NOTE:2] (the seventh month).
notes: The festival. This was the Feast of Tabernacles, see Lev 23:34.
The month Ethanim. This would be September-October in modern reckoning.

verses.zh: 以色列长老来到，祭司便抬起约柜，
verses.en: When all Israel’s elders had arrived, the priests lifted the ark.

verses.zh: 祭司和利未人将耶和华的约柜运上来，又将会幕和会幕的一切圣器具都带上来。
verses.en: The priests and Levites carried the ark of the Lord, the tent of meeting,[NOTE:1] and all the holy items in the tent.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “the tent of assembly.”sn The tent of meeting. See Exod 33:7-11.
Heb “and they carried the ark of the Lord…. The priests and the Levites carried them.”

verses.zh: 所罗门王和聚集到他那里的以色列全会众，一同在约柜前献牛羊为祭，多得不可胜数。
verses.en: Now King Solomon and all the Israelites who had assembled with him went on ahead of the ark and sacrificed more sheep and cattle than could be counted or numbered.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “And King Solomon and all the assembly of Israel, those who had been gathered to him, [were] before the ark, sacrificing sheep and cattle which could not be counted or numbered because of the abundance.”

verses.zh: 祭司将耶和华的约柜抬进内殿，就是至圣所，放在两个基路伯的翅膀底下。
verses.en: The priests brought the ark of the Lord’s covenant to its assigned[NOTE:1] place in the inner sanctuary of the temple, in the Most Holy Place, under the wings of the cherubim.
notes: The word “assigned” is supplied in the translation for clarification.

verses.zh: 基路伯张着翅膀在约柜之上，遮掩约柜和抬柜的杠。
verses.en: The cherubim’s wings extended over the place where the ark sat; the cherubim overshadowed the ark and its poles.[NOTE:1]
notes: And its poles. These poles were used to carry the ark. See Exod 25:13-15.

verses.zh: 这杠甚长，杠头在内殿前的圣所可以看见，在殿外却不能看见，直到如今还在那里。
verses.en: The poles were so long their ends were visible from the Holy Place in front of the inner sanctuary, but they could not be seen from beyond that point.[NOTE:1] They have remained there to this very day.
notes: Heb “they could not be seen outside.”

verses.zh: 约柜里惟有两块石版，就是以色列人出埃及地后，耶和华与他们立约的时候摩西在何烈山所放的。除此以外，并无别物。
verses.en: There was nothing in the ark except the two stone tablets Moses had placed there in Horeb.[NOTE:1] It was there that[NOTE:2] the Lord made a covenant with the Israelites after he brought them out of the land of Egypt.
notes: Horeb is another name for Mount Sinai.
Heb “in Horeb where.”

verses.zh: 祭司从圣所出来的时候，有云充满耶和华的殿；
verses.en: Once the priests left the Holy Place, a cloud filled the Lord’s temple.

verses.zh: 甚至祭司不能站立供职，因为耶和华的荣光充满了殿。
verses.en: The priests could not carry out their duties[NOTE:1] because of the cloud; the Lord’s glory filled his temple.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “were not able to stand to serve.”
Heb “the house of the Lord.”

verses.zh: 那时所罗门说：耶和华曾说，他必住在幽暗之处。
verses.en: Then Solomon said, “The Lord has said that he lives in thick darkness.

verses.zh: 我已经建造殿宇作你的居所，为你永远的住处。
verses.en: O Lord,[NOTE:1] truly I have built a lofty temple for you, a place where you can live permanently.”
notes: The words “O Lord” do not appear in the original text, but they are supplied for clarification; Solomon addresses the Lord in prayer at this point.

verses.zh: 王转脸为以色列会众祝福，以色列会众就都站立。
verses.en: Then the king turned around[NOTE:1] and pronounced a blessing over the whole Israelite assembly as they stood there.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “turned his face.”
Heb “and he blessed all the assembly of Israel, and all the assembly of Israel was standing.”

verses.zh: 所罗门说：「耶和华―以色列的　神是应当称颂的！因他亲口向我父大卫所应许的，也亲手成就了。
verses.en: He said, “The Lord God of Israel is worthy of praise because he has fulfilled[NOTE:1] what he promised[NOTE:2] my father David.
notes: The Hebrew text reads, “by his hand he has fulfilled.”
The Hebrew text reads, “he promised by his mouth.”

verses.zh: 他说：『自从我领我民以色列出埃及以来，我未曾在以色列各支派中选择一城建造殿宇―为我名的居所，但拣选大卫治理我民以色列。』」
verses.en: He told David,[NOTE:1] ‘Since the day I brought my people Israel out of Egypt, I have not chosen a city from all the tribes of Israel to build a temple in which to live.[NOTE:2] But I have chosen David to lead my people Israel.’
notes: Heb “saying.” The word is carried over from the end of verse 15.

To build a temple in which to live (Heb “to build a house for my name to be there”). In the OT, the word “name” sometimes refers to one’s reputation or honor. The “name” of the Lord sometimes designates the Lord himself, being indistinguishable from the proper name.tn Heb “to build a house for my name to be there.”

verses.zh: 所罗门说：「我父大卫曾立意，要为耶和华―以色列　神的名建殿。
verses.en: Now my father David had a strong desire[NOTE:1] to build a temple to honor the Lord God of Israel.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and it was with the heart of David my father.”

Heb “to build a house for the name of the Lord God of Israel.” The word “name” in the OT sometimes refers to one’s reputation or honor. The “name” of the Lord sometimes designates the Lord himself, being indistinguishable from the proper name.

verses.zh: 耶和华却对我父大卫说：『你立意为我的名建殿，这意思甚好。
verses.en: The Lord told my father David, ‘It is right for you to have a strong desire to build a temple to honor me.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “Because it was with your heart to build a house for my name, you did well that it was with your heart.”

verses.zh: 只是你不可建殿，惟你所生的儿子必为我名建殿。』
verses.en: But you will not build the temple; your very own son will build the temple for my honor.’[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “your son, the one who came out of your body, he will build the temple for my name.”

verses.zh: 现在耶和华成就了他所应许的话，使我接续我父大卫坐以色列的国位，又为耶和华―以色列　神的名建造了殿。
verses.en: The Lord has kept the promise he made.[NOTE:1] I have taken my father David’s place and have occupied the throne of Israel, as the Lord promised. I have built this temple for the honor[NOTE:2] of the Lord God of Israel
notes: Heb “his word that he spoke.”
Heb “name.”

verses.zh: 我也在其中为约柜预备一处。约柜内有耶和华的约，就是他领我们列祖出埃及地的时候，与他们所立的约。」
verses.en: and set up in it a place for the ark containing the covenant the Lord made with our ancestors[NOTE:1] when he brought them out of the land of Egypt.”
notes: Heb “fathers” (also in vv. 34, 40, 48, 53, 57, 58).

verses.zh: 所罗门当着以色列会众，站在耶和华的坛前，向天举手说：
verses.en: Solomon stood before the altar of the Lord in front of the entire assembly of Israel and spread out his hands toward the sky.[NOTE:1]
notes: Or “heaven.”

verses.zh: 「耶和华―以色列的　神啊，天上地下没有神可比你的！你向那尽心行在你面前的仆人守约施慈爱；
verses.en: He prayed:[NOTE:1] “O Lord, God of Israel, there is no god like you in heaven above or on earth below! You maintain covenantal loyalty[NOTE:2] to your servants who obey you with sincerity.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “said.”
Heb “one who keeps the covenant and the loyal love.” The expression is a hendiadys.
Heb “who walk before you with all their heart.”

verses.zh: 向你仆人―我父大卫所应许的话现在应验了。你亲口应许，亲手成就，正如今日一样。
verses.en: You have kept your word to your servant, my father David;[NOTE:1] this very day you have fulfilled what you promised.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “[you] who kept to your servant David my father that which you spoke to him.”
Heb “you spoke by your mouth and by your hand you fulfilled, as this day.”

verses.zh: 耶和华―以色列的　神啊，你所应许你仆人―我父大卫的话说：『你的子孙若谨慎自己的行为，在我面前行事像你所行的一样，就不断人坐以色列的国位。』现在求你应验这话。
verses.en: Now, O Lord, God of Israel, keep the promise you made to your servant, my father David, when you said, ‘You will never fail to have a successor ruling before me on the throne of Israel,[NOTE:1] provided that your descendants watch their step[NOTE:2] and serve me as you have done.’[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “there will not be cut off from you a man from before me sitting on the throne of Israel.”
Heb “watch their way.” The Hebrew and English colloquialisms are similar. The related ideas “way” and “steps” represent behavior in a broad sense in each language.
Heb “guard their way by walking before me as you have walked before me.”

verses.zh: 以色列的　神啊，求你成就向你仆人―我父大卫所应许的话。
verses.en: Now, O God of Israel, may the promise you made[NOTE:1] to your servant, my father David, be realized.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “the words that you spoke.”
Or “prove to be reliable.”

verses.zh: 「　神果真住在地上吗？看哪，天和天上的天尚且不足你居住的，何况我所建的这殿呢？
verses.en: “God does not really live on the earth![NOTE:1] Look, if the sky and the highest heaven cannot contain you, how much less this temple I have built!
notes: Heb “Indeed, can God really live on the earth?” The rhetorical question expects the answer, “Of course not,” the force of which the translation above seeks to reflect.

verses.zh: 惟求耶和华―我的　神垂顾仆人的祷告祈求，俯听仆人今日在你面前的祈祷呼吁。
verses.en: But respond favorably to[NOTE:1] your servant’s prayer and his request for help, O Lord my God. Answer[NOTE:2] the desperate prayer[NOTE:3] your servant is presenting to you[NOTE:4] today.
notes: Heb “turn to.”
Heb “by listening to.”
Heb “the loud cry and the prayer.”
Heb “praying before you.”

verses.zh: 愿你昼夜看顾这殿，就是你应许立为你名的居所；求你垂听仆人向此处祷告的话。
verses.en: Night and day may you watch over this temple, the place where you promised you would live.[NOTE:1] May you answer your servant’s prayer for this place.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “so your eyes might be open toward this house night and day, toward the place about which you said, ‘My name will be there.’”
Heb “by listening to the prayer which your servant is praying concerning this place.”

verses.zh: 你仆人和你民以色列向此处祈祷的时候，求你在天上你的居所垂听，垂听而赦免。
verses.en: Respond to the request of your servant and your people Israel for this place.[NOTE:1] Hear from inside your heavenly dwelling place[NOTE:2] and respond favorably.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “listen to the request of your servant and your people Israel which they are praying concerning this place.”

Heb “and you, hear inside your dwelling place, inside heaven.” The precise nuance of the preposition אֶל (ʾel), used here with the verb “hear,” is unclear. One expects the preposition “from,” which appears in the parallel text in 2 Chr 6:21. The nuance “inside; among” is attested for אֶל (see Gen 23:19; 1 Sam 10:22; Jer 4:3), but in each case a verb of motion is employed with the preposition, unlike 1 Kgs 8:30. The translation above (“from inside”) is based on the demands of the immediate context rather than attested usage elsewhere.
Heb “hear and forgive.”

verses.zh: 「人若得罪邻舍，有人叫他起誓，他来到这殿在你的坛前起誓，
verses.en: “When someone is accused of sinning against his neighbor and the latter pronounces a curse on the alleged offender before your altar in this temple, be willing to forgive the accused if the accusation is false.[NOTE:1]
notes: Be willing to forgive the accused if the accusation is false. At first it appears that Solomon is asking God to forgive the guilty party. But in v. 32 Solomon asks the Lord to discern who is guilty and innocent, so v. 31 must refer to a situation where an accusation has been made, but not yet proven. The very periphrastic translation reflects this interpretation.tn Heb “and forgive the man who sins against his neighbor when one takes up against him a curse to curse him and the curse comes before your altar in this house.” In the Hebrew text the words “and forgive” conclude v. 30, but the accusative sign at the beginning of v. 31 suggests the verb actually goes with what follows in v. 31. The parallel text in 2 Chr 6:22 begins with “and if,” rather than the accusative sign. In this case “forgive” must be taken with what precedes, and v. 31 must be taken as the protasis (“if” clause) of a conditional sentence, with v. 32 being the apodosis (“then” clause) that completes the sentence.

verses.zh: 求你在天上垂听，判断你的仆人：定恶人有罪，照他所行的报应在他头上；定义人有理，照他的义赏赐他。
verses.en: Listen from heaven and make a just decision about your servants’ claims. Condemn the guilty party, declare the other innocent, and give both of them what they deserve.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and you, hear [from] heaven and act and judge your servants by declaring the guilty to be guilty, to give his way on his head, and to declare the innocent to be innocent, to give to him according to his innocence.”

verses.zh: 「你的民以色列若得罪你，败在仇敌面前，又归向你，承认你的名，在这殿里祈求祷告，
verses.en: “The time will come when[NOTE:1] your people Israel are defeated by an enemy[NOTE:2] because they sinned against you. If they come back to you, renew their allegiance to you,[NOTE:3] and pray for your help[NOTE:4] in this temple,
notes: Heb “when.” In the Hebrew text vv. 33-34 actually contain one lengthy conditional sentence, which the translation has divided into two sentences for stylistic reasons.
Or “are struck down before an enemy.”
Heb “confess [or perhaps, “praise”] your name.”
Heb “and they pray and ask for help.”

verses.zh: 求你在天上垂听，赦免你民以色列的罪，使他们归回你赐给他们列祖之地。
verses.en: then listen from heaven, forgive the sin of your people Israel, and bring them back to the land you gave to their ancestors.

verses.zh: 「你的民因得罪你，你惩罚他们，使天闭塞不下雨；他们若向此处祷告，承认你的名，离开他们的罪，
verses.en: “The time will come when[NOTE:1] the skies are shut up tightly and no rain falls because your people[NOTE:2] sinned against you. When they direct their prayers toward this place, renew their allegiance to you,[NOTE:3] and turn away from their sin because you punish[NOTE:4] them,
notes: Heb “when.” In the Hebrew text vv. 35-36a actually contain one lengthy conditional sentence, which the translation has divided into two sentences for stylistic reasons.
Heb “they”; the referent (your people) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “confess [or perhaps, “praise”] your name.”

The Hebrew text has “because you answer them,” as if the verb is from עָנָה (ʿanah, “to answer”). However, this reference to a divine answer is premature, since the next verse asks for God to intervene in mercy. It is better to revocalize the consonantal text as תְעַנֵּם (teʿannem, “you afflict them”), a Piel verb form from the homonym עָנָה (ʿanah, “to afflict”).

verses.zh: 求你在天上垂听，赦免你仆人以色列民的罪，将当行的善道指教他们，且降雨在你的地，就是你赐给你民为业之地。
verses.en: then listen from heaven and forgive the sin of your servants, your people Israel. Certainly[NOTE:1] you will then teach them the right way to live[NOTE:2] and send rain on your land that you have given your people to possess.[NOTE:3]
notes: The translation understands כִּי (ki) in an emphatic or asseverative sense.
Heb “the good way in which they should walk.”
Or “for an inheritance.”

verses.zh: 「国中若有饥荒、瘟疫、旱风、霉烂、蝗虫、蚂蚱，或有仇敌犯境围困城邑，无论遭遇甚么灾祸疾病，
verses.en: “The time will come when the land suffers from a famine, a plague, blight and disease, or a locust[NOTE:1] invasion, or when their enemy lays siege to the cities of the land,[NOTE:2] or when some other type of plague or epidemic occurs.
notes: Actually two Hebrew terms appear here, both of which are usually taken as referring to locusts. Perhaps different stages of growth or different varieties are in view.
Heb “in the land, his gates.”

verses.zh: 你的民以色列，或是众人，或是一人，自觉有罪（原文是灾），向这殿举手，无论祈求甚么，祷告甚么，
verses.en: When all your people Israel pray and ask for help,[NOTE:1] as they acknowledge their pain[NOTE:2] and spread out their hands toward this temple,
notes: Heb “every prayer, every request for help which will be to all the people, to all your people Israel.”
Heb “which they know, each the pain of his heart.”

verses.zh: 求你在天上你的居所垂听赦免。你是知道人心的，要照各人所行的待他们（惟有你知道世人的心），
verses.en: then listen from your heavenly dwelling place, forgive their sin,[NOTE:1] and act favorably toward each one based on your evaluation of his motives.[NOTE:2] (Indeed you are the only one who can correctly evaluate the motives of all people.)[NOTE:3]
notes: The words “their sin” are added for clarification.

Heb “and act and give to each one according to all his ways because you know his heart.” In the Hebrew text vv. 37-39a actually contain one lengthy conditional sentence, which the translation has divided up for stylistic reasons.
Heb “Indeed you know, you alone, the heart of all the sons of mankind.”

verses.zh: 使他们在你赐给我们列祖之地上一生一世敬畏你。
verses.en: Then they will obey[NOTE:1] you throughout their lifetimes as[NOTE:2] they live on the land you gave to our ancestors.
notes: Heb “fear.”
Heb “all the days [in] which.”

verses.zh: 「论到不属你民以色列的外邦人，为你名从远方而来，
verses.en: “Foreigners, who do not belong to your people Israel, will come from a distant land because of your reputation.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “your name.” In the OT the word “name” sometimes refers to one’s reputation or honor. The “name” of the Lord sometimes designates the Lord himself, being indistinguishable from the proper name.

verses.zh: （他们听人论说你的大名和大能的手，并伸出来的膀臂）向这殿祷告，
verses.en: When they hear about your great reputation[NOTE:1] and your ability to accomplish mighty deeds,[NOTE:2] they will come and direct their prayers toward this temple.
notes: Heb “your great name.” See the note on the word “reputation” in the previous verse.
Heb “and your strong hand and your outstretched arm.”

verses.zh: 求你在天上你的居所垂听，照着外邦人所祈求的而行，使天下万民都认识你的名，敬畏你像你的民以色列一样；又使他们知道我建造的这殿是称为你名下的。
verses.en: Then listen from your heavenly dwelling place and answer all the prayers of the foreigners.[NOTE:1] Then all the nations of the earth will acknowledge your reputation,[NOTE:2] obey[NOTE:3] you as your people Israel do, and recognize that this temple I built belongs to you.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “and do all which the foreigner calls to [i.e., “requests of”] you.”
Heb “your name.” See the note on the word “reputation” in v. 41.
Heb “fear.”
Heb “that your name is called over this house which I built.” The Hebrew idiom “to call the name over” indicates ownership. See 2 Sam 12:28.

verses.zh: 「你的民若奉你的差遣，无论往何处去与仇敌争战，向耶和华所选择的城与我为你名所建造的殿祷告，
verses.en: “When you direct your people to march out and fight their enemies,[NOTE:1] and they direct their prayers to the Lord[NOTE:2] toward his chosen city and this temple I built for your honor,[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “When your people go out for battle against their enemies in the way which you send them.”
Or perhaps “to you, O Lord.” See 2 Chr 6:34.
Heb “your name.” See the note on the word “reputation” in v. 41.

verses.zh: 求你在天上垂听他们的祷告祈求，使他们得胜。
verses.en: then listen from heaven to their prayers for help[NOTE:1] and vindicate them.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “their prayer and their request for help.”
Heb “and accomplish their justice.”

verses.zh: 「你的民若得罪你（世上没有不犯罪的人），你向他们发怒，将他们交给仇敌掳到仇敌之地，或远或近，
verses.en: “The time will come when your people[NOTE:1] will sin against you (for there is no one who is sinless!) and you will be angry with them and deliver them over to their enemies, who will take them as prisoners to their own land,[NOTE:2] whether far away or close by.
notes: Heb “they”; the referent (your people) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “the land of the enemy.”

verses.zh: 他们若在掳到之地想起罪来，回心转意，恳求你说：『我们有罪了，我们悖逆了，我们作恶了』；
verses.en: When your people[NOTE:1] come to their senses[NOTE:2] in the land where they are held prisoner, they will repent and beg for your mercy in the land of their imprisonment, admitting, ‘We have sinned and gone astray;[NOTE:3] we have done evil.’
notes: Heb “they”; the referent (your people) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Or “stop and reflect”; Heb “bring back to their heart.”
Or “done wrong.”

verses.zh: 他们若在掳到之地尽心尽性归服你，又向自己的地，就是你赐给他们列祖之地和你所选择的城，并我为你名所建造的殿祷告，
verses.en: When they return to you with all their heart and being[NOTE:1] in the land[NOTE:2] where they are held prisoner, and direct their prayers to you toward the land you gave to their ancestors, your chosen city, and the temple I built for your honor,[NOTE:3]
notes: Or “soul.”
Heb “in the land of their enemies.”
Heb “your name.” See the note on the word “reputation” in v. 41.

verses.zh: 求你在天上你的居所垂听他们的祷告祈求，为他们伸冤；
verses.en: then listen from your heavenly dwelling place to their prayers for help[NOTE:1] and vindicate them.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “their prayer and their request for help.”
Heb “and accomplish their justice.”

verses.zh: 饶恕得罪你的民，赦免他们的一切过犯，使他们在掳他们的人面前蒙怜恤。
verses.en: Forgive all the rebellious acts of your sinful people and cause their captors to have mercy on them.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and forgive your people who have sinned against you, and all their rebellious acts by which they rebelled against you, and grant them mercy before their captors so they will show them mercy.”

verses.zh: 因为他们是你的子民，你的产业，是你从埃及领出来脱离铁炉的。
verses.en: After all,[NOTE:1] they are your people and your special possession[NOTE:2] whom you brought out of Egypt, from the middle of the iron-smelting furnace.[NOTE:3]
notes: Or “for.”
Heb “inheritance.”

From the middle of the iron-smelting furnace. The metaphor of a furnace suggests fire and heat and is an apt image to remind the people of the suffering they endured while slaves in Egypt.tn The Hebrew term כּוּר (kur, “furnace,” cf. Akkadian kūru) is a metaphor for the intense heat of purification. A כּוּר was not a source of heat but a crucible (“iron-smelting furnace”) in which precious metals were melted down and their impurities burned away (see I. Cornelius, NIDOTTE 2:618-19). Thus Egypt served not as a place of punishment for the Israelites, but as a place of refinement to bring Israel to a place of submission to divine sovereignty.

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own

You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects. Compare your subject divisions with the five translations

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- This chapter is very repetitive in its phrasing (much of which is like Deuteronomy). It deals with different categories

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE ARK OF THE COVENANT

8:2 "the feast" There were several feasts of the seventh month.

- Rosh Hashanah (new year feast)

- Yom Kippur (day of atonement)

- Sukkot (feast of tabernacles or booths)

What surprises commentators is that 2 Kgs. 6:38 says that the temple was finished in the eighth month,
but here that it was dedicated in the eleventh month. Why the delay is not known, only speculated. This appears to be
the Feast of Tabernacles or Booths (cf. Lev. 23:34; Deut. 16:13-15; 1 Kgs. 8:21; 12:32; 2 Chr. 5:3; 7:8; Neh. 8:14;

- the lampstand

- the table of show bread

▣ "the cloud" This was a visible sign of YHWH's presence with Israel during the exodus and wilderness
wanderings. It dissipated when Israel crossed the Jordan into Canaan.

This refers to the special cloud ("pillar," BDB 765) representing YHWH's personal presence that led
and protected the Hebrew slaves as they left Egypt and wandered in the wilderness (cf. Exod. 13:21-22; 14:19,24; 33:9,10;
Deut. 1:33; Neh. 9:12,19; Ps. 78:14; 105:39). This cloud/pillar disappeared after the Israelites crossed the Jordan River
into the Promised Land. This was called the "Shekinah Cloud of Glory" by the rabbis (cf. Exod. 13:21-22; 14:19,24; 33:9-10;
Ps. 78:14; 99:7). It accomplished several things for the Israelites.

- symbol of YHWH's personal presence (shekinah means "to dwell with")

- it separated Israel from Pharaoh's elite troops (cf. Exod. 14:19-20)

- it led Israel (cf. Exod. 13:21-22; Num. 9:17-23)

- it covered them and protected them from the heat (cf. Ps. 105:39)

- it lit up the camp by night, even allowed Israel to travel at night (cf. Exod. 13:21; Neh. 9:12,19)

- it caused the nations to fear Israel (cf. Exod. 23:27; Deut. 2:25; 11:25; Josh. 2:9)

- it finally disappeared when Israel crossed the Jordan (cf. Exod. 16:35; Josh. 5:12), but reappeared at the dedication
of Solomon's temple (1 Kings 8)

The NT also uses this imagery as the transportation of Deity (i.e., Acts 1:9; 1 Thess. 4:17), following
Daniel 7:13.

Here is my exegetical note from Deut. 12:5:

Deut. 12:5 "the place which the Lord your God shall choose" God chose
(BDB 103, KB 119, Qal IMPERFECT, cf. vv. 11,14,18,21,26; 14:25; 15:20; 16:2,6,11,15;

The tabernacle (ark) traveled with Israel:

- Gilgal, Josh. 4:19; 10:6,15

- Shechem, Josh 8:33

- Shiloh, Josh 18:1; Jdgs. 18:31; 1 Sam. 1:3

- Bethel, (possible) Jdgs. 20:18,26-28; 21:2

- Jerusalem

- David brings the ark to Jerusalem (cf. 2 Samuel 6)

- David purchases the site of the temple (2 Sam. 24:15-25; 2 Chr. 3:1)

Many modern scholars have tried to assert that Deuteronomy was written late to accommodate
Hezekiah and Josiah's reforms of centralizing Israel's worship. However, Deuteronomy does not name Jerusalem
as the specific site that YHWH will choose. In context the theological contrast is between:

- the local Ba'al shrines and the one shrine of Israel

- the monotheism of Israel versus the polytheism of Canaan (and the rest of the Ancient Near East)

SPECIAL TOPIC: HE CHOSE US.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEART.

8:65 "the feast" See full note at 1 Kgs. 8:2.

▣ "from the entrance of Hamath to the brook of Egypt" This was a way of referring to all of Solomon's
